subject.title: [Bug]: Enabling Codex plugin causes Runtime to switch to OpenAI Codex and ignore configured primary model, resulting in GPT-5.4-nano TPM failures

question: Should this issue remain a standalone DeepSeek-plus-Codex hot-reload bug, or should maintainers consolidate it under the shared session model/runtime resolver work?
rationale: The evidence supports a real provider/session-state failure class, but the safe fix depends on maintainer intent around explicit /model pins, auto-fallback cleanup, and the OpenAI Codex default runtime boundary.

options.title: Keep As Standalone Repro
options.body: Keep this issue open as the user-facing DeepSeek/Codex repro while using https://github.com/openclaw/openclaw/issues/87957 as the architecture owner and https://github.com/openclaw/openclaw/issues/101672 for doctor repair evidence.

options.title: Consolidate Under Resolver
options.body: Close this later as a duplicate only after maintainers confirm the reporter's logs are preserved on https://github.com/openclaw/openclaw/issues/87957 and no distinct hot-reload trigger remains.

options.title: Narrow To Doctor Gap
options.body: Treat this as covered by https://github.com/openclaw/openclaw/issues/101672 only if maintainers confirm persisted auto fallback route state, not plugin enablement, is the full root cause.

recommendation.title: Keep As Standalone Repro
recommendation.body: Keep this issue open as the user-facing DeepSeek/Codex repro while using https://github.com/openclaw/openclaw/issues/87957 as the architecture owner and https://github.com/openclaw/openclaw/issues/101672 for doctor repair evidence.

likelyOwner.reason: The recent OpenAI provider unification touched the runtime/provider boundary and docs that frame this decision.
